lesson_title: The Syllabus on Your Shelves: Nine Acids and Bases
hook_text: Four acids and five bases decide a whole chemistry chapter — and you own almost all of them already.
clip_script: Begin at the kitchen counter. The vinegar bottle holds ethanoic acid, CH3COOH — edible only because it is weak, stingy with its one loose hydrogen. Beside it, baking soda: sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO3, the gentle base that lifts a sponge cake and settles an aching stomach. The laundry shelf: washing soda, sodium carbonate, Na2CO3 — the burlier sibling of baking soda, carrying two sodiums. Under the sink, drain cleaner: sodium hydroxide, caustic soda — a base fierce enough to digest a hair clog. The eye-watering window spray: ammonia, NH3 — the base that walks past the doorman with no hydroxide on its guest pass. Out to the garage. The white bottle of pool acid: hydrochloric acid — chemically identical to the acid your stomach brews before lunch. The car battery: sulphuric acid, H2SO4, the only one carrying two acidic hydrogens. And here is the real secret: you never memorise these formulae. You build them — charges snap together like magnets until the total hits zero. Nine substances. One house. Marks waiting.
visual_style: Room-by-room house walkthrough where each product bottle freezes and its formula stamps across the label; finale of ion tiles clicking together magnetically until a zero lights up.
mood: Homely and eye-opening — the exam list discovered on the viewer's own shelves.
pacing: Brisk room hops with one freeze-frame each, a pause on the ammonia impostor, magnet-snap ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn your own house into a formula sheet.
